- Budget target: procurement has given us a target blended unit cost of ~$700 per 1M tokens. That’s the upper bound for finance approval.
- Routes/models: our plan is to add two new routes in Q3 — one embeddings-heavy (vector search) and one gen-heavy (customer-facing summaries). We want to understand blended impact if embeddings (lower cost per token) and gen (higher cost) are combined under the same committed tiers.

Hi Sanjay —

Great — thanks for the clear targets. Per your ask I’ve included a short worked example below (full workbook attached).

Example blended math (illustrative):
- Committed tier: 50M tokens/month committed for months 1–3, stepping to 75M for months 4–6, 100M for months 7–12.
- Unit list rates (examples): Gen-heavy route = $1,200 / 1M tokens; Embedding route = $300 / 1M tokens.
- Discount tiers applied to list for committed volume: 10% @ 50M, 20% @ 75M, 30% @ 100M.

Month 7 example (100M committed):
- If traffic mix is 70% gen / 30% embeddings:
   - Gen effective rate = 1200 * (1 - 0.30) = $840 / 1M
   - Embedding effective rate = 300 * (1 - 0.30) = $210 / 1M
   - Blended = 0.7 * 840 + 0.3 * 210 = $651 / 1M tokens

That blended example gets under your $700/1M target at the 100M committed tier. If committed volume is lower, blended goes up (see tab "Blended Scenarios").

Notes/assumptions:
- We treat routes as token-in/token-out for tier math (you can choose to partition tiers by route if you prefer separate commitments).
- New routes added mid-term can be added under the same tier with an addendum; pricing for new routes follows the same discount schedule unless you choose to carve out specific route pricing.
- Embedded inference (low-latency vector search) tends to be materially cheaper — we can apply an SLO-based discount if high-throughput caching is acceptable.

Looping Rishi on the technical implications of the routes and whether quantization/accelerators change the offered effective rates. Rishi — can you confirm the assumptions on typical cost delta for embeddings vs gen and any recommended route-level controls?

Next: once you confirm which model mix you expect at each tier I’ll produce a final proposal and a term summary for Procurement.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Renewal & expansion pricing: volume step-ups, blended rates, new model routes

Hi all —

Quick technical notes to supplement Marissa’s pricing math:
- Embeddings routes (vector generation) typically run on smaller models and quantized kernels which reduce GPU time per token by ~60–80% vs gen-heavy routes. That lines up to the example 300 vs 1200 list numbers Marissa used.
- If Acme enables prefix/KV caching for your gen routes and uses batch sizes tuned to 8–16, we commonly see an additional ~15–20% effective cost reduction.
- For new routes we recommend: mark them as separate "route ids" in the contract so usage can be attributed and blended calculations updated automatically. It keeps billing transparent and makes add-ons easier.
- If you require a strict blended floor for finance (e.g., not to exceed $700/1M), we can set an escalation clause that adjusts discounts at predefined usage thresholds.

Happy to jump on a quick call with your infra/procurement folks to walk through the technical tradeoffs.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
